questions.q: What are life processes? Describe nutrition and respiration in animals.
answer: Life processes are the basic functions that keep an organism alive — nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion.

answer.text: Animals are heterotrophs that take in ready-made food. Nutrition involves ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion. In humans, food passes from the mouth through the oesophagus to the stomach and small intestine, where it is digested and absorbed through villi, before waste leaves through the large intestine and anus.

Respiration breaks down food in the cells to release energy. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and releases more energy, while anaerobic respiration works without oxygen and releases less. Humans respire using lungs, fish through gills, and insects through spiracles and tracheae.

questions.q: Describe circulation and excretion in the human body.

answer.text: The circulatory system transports materials around the body. The heart pumps blood, which carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin in the red blood cells, along with digested food and wastes. Blood travels away from the heart through arteries, returns through veins, and exchanges materials with cells through tiny capillaries.

Excretion is the removal of wastes produced by the body. The kidneys filter wastes such as urea from the blood to form urine, which passes through the ureters to the urinary bladder and out through the urethra. Sweat from the skin also removes some water and salts.

answer: Together these processes keep the body supplied and clean.
